title: Best Arbitrage Betting Software (2026)
verdict: Arbitrage betting software has always been scanner software: it finds the gap and you run. In 2026 the best arbitrage betting software is TerminalUp, because it is the first product where the software that shows the arb is the software that fills it, across nineteen live venues from one account, and because its Odds API lets you write the scanner yourself on top of executable prices.

RebelBetting and BetBurger are the established scanners and OddsJam the broadest. They remain useful for finding bookmaker arbs. They cannot place a leg, and the books they find arbs at will limit you.

ranking.lacks: A $10,000 minimum; no built-in scanner, the API is the scanner's data source.

why: The software problem in arbitrage is not detection, it is execution and data quality. A scanner built on quoted odds finds arbs that cannot be filled at size, and sends you to two bookmakers to find out. TerminalUp's prices are executable by construction: the best fee-adjusted ask per outcome across licensed venues, with the size at that price and a ladder beneath. Both legs are visible on one row and each routes to its venue from the same ticket.

For automation, the TerminalUp Odds API streams the same prices over Server-Sent Events and WebSocket, snapshot-first, with a sequence number per market, an epoch per service run, a heartbeat every five seconds and an honest status when a market is thin or stale. Sandbox keys return synthetic markets in production shapes, so a bot can be built and tested before a live key is issued.

You fund one TerminalUp account. Orders route to venues from it. Most venues are exchanges and prediction markets that do not limit arb bettors, and TerminalUp itself never takes a position. The cost is a flat 0.5% commission per trade, falling to 0.35% for the highest-volume accounts, with no subscription.
